newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads - Mixed after U.S. sell off.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads - Mixed after U.S. sell off.

text.p: Australian bond spreads put in a mixed performance on a holiday affected Monday, outperforming a bearish Treasuries market, but losing some ground against other dollar bloc debt.
Bonds weakened markedly after Treasuries were sold down sharply on Friday, and remained at the lower levels through holiday affected trade on Monday.
Trade was thinned by the closure of the Sydney Futures Exchange for a bank holiday in New South Wales, with futures trading limited to the SYCOM system, normally used for after hours trading.
While outperforming Treasuries on the day, bond spreads widened to long Canandian and New Zealand debt.

New Zealand bonds outperformed on market confidence that Tuesday's June quarter labour report will be weak, and therefore could force the RBNZ to allow the easier monetary conditions the market has been testing in the past few days.
The short end was the best performer on the day, down by seven points to the long end's 15 late in the day. As a result, the yield curve reversed Thursday and Friday's flattening.
